display_name: The monthly net income, in a month of 2026, of a household with one employed parent: income tax for tax year 2026 and its twelfth, national insurance deducted from the salary, the child allowance and the net, composed from eight rows (IL-01 to IL-06 and both halves of IL-08) encoding the Income Tax Ordinance and the National Insurance Law

run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from BRIEF.md

v0.2.0.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents: integration of row IL-08, as ruled by Meng on 2026-10-07 (integrate rather than repair the earlier rows)

v0.2.1.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents: the Schedule J switch moved into rows IL-04 and IL-05 (both v0.3.0), and the capstone made to follow IL-04's

v0.2.2.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents: row IL-04's fork F6 made a switch (its v0.4.0, a fall declined by default); the capstone re-vendored IL-04's two changed modules, no capstone module changed

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English (@lang en). The few Hebrew runs are copied from the two deposited sources and cited by line.

composes.provisions: NII s 1 (as needed), ss 334, 337, Schedule J (v0.3.0: the Schedule J switch, fork F4 ruled; v0.4.0: fork F6 a switch, a fall in the index or the average wage declined by default; the capstone does not reach it)
NII Schedule K, ss 342, 348 (v0.3.0: s 342(c) at a reading of Schedule J)
ITO ss 35, 37-39, 40(b), 45A, 47 (with s 47(a)), 64B (vendored, not composed), 65; the Tax Authority's 2026 figures for ss 45A and 47
NII s 72, s 335, Schedule A1 Part D

vendoring: The l4 CLI cannot import across directories, so vendor.sh copies the rows' 50 rule, noun and published-figure modules (36 of rows IL-01 to IL-06, 10 of IL-08's Income Tax Ordinance half, 4 of its National Insurance Law half) flat into this directory (git-ignored) and VENDORED.sha256 pins each by sha256, row and commons commit; check.sh runs vendor.sh --check first. Each il07-adapter-il0N.l4 (and il07-adapter-il08-ito.l4, il07-adapter-il08-nii.l4) imports this row's nouns and one row only. See RECONCILE.md section 1.
scope: Answered: months of 2026, for a household with one employed parent paid the same salary every month of 2026, possibly a spouse with no income, and the parent's own children. Composed: the s 121 tax and the s 121B additional tax (IL-03) on the year's income (under ITO s 65, IL-08, where the couple is assessed together in the earner's name), less the credit points of ss 34, 36, 36A (IL-01), s 35 (IL-08), s 66(c) in a separate calculation with s 37's point halved (IL-02, IL-08), ss 37-39 under s 65 (IL-08), s 40(b) for a parent without a spouse (IL-08), at the 2026 credit-point value from s 120B(e)(1) (IL-03) and the Tax Authority's 2025 figure (IL-01), and the s 45A credit (IL-08); one twelfth of it (fork K1); the employer's deduction under NII s 342(c) (IL-05) of Schedule J column D (IL-04), read at its printed totals by Meng's ruling of 2026-10-07, through row IL-04's own switch from 0.2.1 (the items' reading kept as fork K14; K18) on the s 348 income (IL-05) in the branches s 335 gives (IL-08), with a woman's Schedule A1 Part D age (IL-08); the child allowance under NII ss 65-68 (IL-06) for the children s 72 pays for in the month (IL-08), with the s 66 additional-tax exclusion joined to IL-03's s 121B (fork K5). Inputs, not encoded: the health insurance contribution (National Health Insurance Law), the registered spouse (ITO s 64B is encoded by IL-08 but reads facts the household does not hold), residence and insurance statuses, and, in the further facts of version 0.2.0, the pension contributions and insurance premiums, immigration, the statuses ss 37 and 335 read, and the single-parent facts. Declined by name: every month outside 2026; a spouse with income; a couple assessed under ITO s 65 in the other spouse's name; a parent without a spouse whose single-parent facts are not given; an earner with a credit or deduction no row encodes (ss 39A-40D, 44-46 and the like); a salary that varies across the year (ITO s 164 and its Regulations); a month for which s 72 pays children row IL-06 counts together on no day (an 18th birthday on the 1st); where s 47 would deduct anything; the deduction of an earner who does not pay in all six deduction branches, at the printed totals; every place a known defect of row IL-08 could change the answer (its findings D187, D183, D190/D236, D055 and observation 1); the rows' own refusals. GAPS.md has the status of every gap.

published_figures.source: Israel Tax Authority monthly withholding booklet 2026, PDF p. 8, Internet Archive capture 20260207101513, sha256 282bb886ccae1cc718840127af378fce88ca37ee3b2b9f00ed2cd44467e86285 (il07-published-figures.l4)

expected_red.why: R2 (1): row IL-02's s 66(c)(4) half point under s 36A is 0.5 for a resident foreign-worker woman where row IL-01 declines s 36A under s 48A. R3 (1, added in 0.2.0): row IL-08's s 45A credit for survivors' insurance cut by the 1.5% proviso falls below the s 45A(d)(1) floor (its independent finding D187): 611.1 where the text gives 793.8. R1 (the Institute's 7% against IL-04's items) was resolved in 0.2.1, when row IL-04 v0.3.0 took the printed totals by default; its two assertions were removed. NOTES.md sections 6, 11.14.

The independent tests of fid-il-07, written against version 0.1.0 and not edited. Against 0.2.0 at the printed totals (Meng's ruling): 258 satisfied. 75 of 0.1.0's 80 failures now pass (F1's 74, now that column D is read at 7% above the threshold, and H43's net, now declined); all 6 refusals now pass (H25, H27, H28 under s 72); 3 failures stand (H43's tax, H45's deduction and net, the tester's own guesses); 2 failures are now refusals (H44n, an 18th birthday on the 1st, fork K15); 15 assertions that passed now fail only on the words of a refusal 0.2.0 reworded because a provision is now encoded or the composed rows are eight (ss 40(b), 35, 45A, 47; the period). NOTES.md sections 11.8 and 11.13.

forks.K1: The year's tax against a month: one twelfth of the year's tax for a salary the same every month (reported as a share, not as tax withheld); declined otherwise, because withholding is ITO s 164 and Regulations not in the sources.
forks.K2: The 2026 credit-point value: IL-03's s 120B(e)(1) from the 1 January 2024 rounded figure, which is the Tax Authority's published 2025 value (2,904, IL-01); twelve times the booklet's monthly 242 agrees.
forks.K3: Credits are set off against the s 121 tax only, never below nil, and the s 121B additional tax is added after; where the credits exceed the s 121 tax and there is additional tax, declined.
forks.K4: The earner's taxable income is the year's salary in every case answered; a spouse with income is declined. (0.2.0) A couple with no separate calculation is assessed under ITO s 65 (row IL-08): answered where the earner is the registered spouse, declined where the other spouse is.
forks.K5: IL-06's 'income chargeable to additional tax' is read for the tax year in which the month falls: TRUE iff IL-03's s 121B tax for that year is above nil.
forks.K6: SUPERSEDED in 0.2.0 by K15. (0.1.0: IL-06 is asked about the first day of the month; a month in which a child is born or turns 18 after that day is declined (NII s 72).)
forks.K7: s 36A's half point is counted once, from IL-01, though IL-02 restates it in s 66(c)(4).
forks.K8: The employee's deduction under NII s 342(c) is a percentage of the s 348 income (Schedule K's maximum and minimum applied), not of the wage paid.
forks.K9: IL-04's column D average-wage argument is not read for 2026; the adapter passes a named refusal there.
forks.K10: The tests' health figure applies the Institute's published employee health rates to the salary up to 51,910; the capstone itself takes the figure as an input.
forks.K11: SUPERSEDED in 0.2.0. (0.1.0: s 37 entitlement is an input, as in IL-02.) Now s 37's own answer (row IL-08) on the statuses it reads; the couple's field must agree with it, and TRUE without the statuses is declined.
forks.K12: (0.2.0) Under ITO s 65 no children's credit points are given: s 66(c)'s are for a separate calculation, s 40(b)'s for a single-parent family (row IL-08's NOTES.md section 6 reads it the same way).
forks.K13: (0.2.0) The net is the brief's: salary less tax/12, national insurance and health, plus the allowance. It does not deduct the earner's own pension contribution, a deposit to the earner's provident fund under neither Law.
forks.K14: (0.2.0) THE SCHEDULE J SWITCH, RULED by Meng on 2026-10-07: above the reduced collection threshold, column D is read at its printed totals by default (7.00 above, 1.04 below; NII Schedule J line 4730; the National Insurance Institute deducts 7%), and the sum of the six deduction branches' items (4.67, lines 4720-4729; row IL-04's fork F4 chose it) is kept as the alternative. The capstone's rule `IL-07: the reading of Schedule J column D the capstone takes` (il07-pipeline.l4) follows row IL-04's own switch from 0.2.1 (fork K18); the other reading is a one-line change in IL-04's nii-schedule-j.l4. At Schedule K's maximum the readings differ by 1,030.0231 a month. Under the printed totals an earner who does not pay in all six deduction branches is declined. NOTES.md section 11.13.
forks.K15: (0.2.0) NII s 72 with IL-06: IL-06 is asked about the children s 72 pays for in the month, on the first day of the month or the latest birthday in it of such a child; where one of them is 18 on that day by IL-06's rule, no day of the month counts them all, and the month's allowance is declined.
forks.K16: (0.2.0) NII s 335 where the caller gives no statuses: an earner resident in Israel and insured under Chapter 11 is taken to be insured in every branch, as 0.1.0 took every employee; any other earner's deduction is declined.
forks.K17: (0.2.0) The ITO s 45A credit, in money, is set off with the credit points against the s 121 tax, no further than to nil, and the s 121B tax added after; declined where the credits exceed the s 121 tax and there is additional tax (as K3). Row IL-08's fork F11 leaves the order to the composer.
forks.K18: (0.2.1) The Schedule J switch is row IL-04's (v0.3.0, backlog row IL-11), with row IL-05's s 342(c) following it; the capstone maps IL-04's reading into its own and passes it to IL-05, with IL-04's column D at the printed totals for the deduction branches together as IL-05's argument. Fewer than all six deduction branches above the threshold are declined by IL-04.
